articleTitle: Demonstration of Secure Key Management Solution with Use Case in Permissioned Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: In a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), it is important to store the private keys in a well-protected storage as they provide ownership and control over the digital assets. The compromise of private keys may bring the security breakdown of the system with no possible recovery. This article focuses on the security considerations of the PKI entities in distributed applications using permissioned blockchain i.e., Hyperledger Fabric (HLF). The PKI based Certificate Authority (CA) in HLF is responsible for identity management in the framework by generating the public-private key pairs and certificates for each entity in the fabric. The private keys of the entities are stored in a readily accessible format. There are various protected storages like hot and cold wallets, secures databases that have been discussed throughout the literature. Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) are the devices that follow defacto cryptographic standard for securing keys in any cryptographic implementation. This paper presents the prototype for integration of our indigenous CA for HLF with HSM. The practical demonstration of the study is done using softHSM an emulation of physical HSM that is available in open source.

articleTitle: Experimenting Integration of Custom ECDSA Algorithm in OpenSSL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: OpenSSL is one of the most widely used cryptographic library for establishing secure communication using transport layer security (TLS) protocols. The crypto library of OpenSSL supports both symmetric (AES) and asymmetric (RSA, ECDSA) cryptographic algorithms. Nowadays the software based secure key storage implementations also use OpenSSL for their cryptographic operations. However, there is need to customize the crypto modules of OpenSSL for two reasons: i) to avoid the proven attacks on OpenSSL crypto implementations ii) integrate the custom crypto implementations in applications like blockchain. In general, there is no reference document for adding new algorithms into OpenSSL. Hence this article summarizes the mechanisms by which custom cryptographic implementations can be added into OpenSSL crypto library and also discusses the pros and cons of every mechanism.

articleTitle: Role of PKI in Securing AMQP Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: The prevalence of IoT devices has introduced significant challenges in securing communication due to the resource-constrained nature of these devices and the need for scalable security solutions. The AMQP is widely used for IoT communication, offering reliable message delivery and interoperability. However, securing AMQP-based IoT communication requires robust mechanisms to ensure data integrity, confidentiality, and authentication. PKI emerges as a key component in addressing security requirements for IoT communications. This research paper delves into the security aspects of AMQP, highlighting both its strengths and vulnerabilities. It underscores how, despite its robust security features like TLS and SASL, AMQP can still be susceptible to targeted attacks. The paper further explores the role of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) in enhancing the security of AMQP communications. By providing a framework for encryption, authentication, and data integrity, PKI plays a crucial role in safeguarding AMQP against potential threats, ensuring that communication remains secure and reliable in various applications.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Zero-Knowledge Proofs: A Through Review and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: Zero Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) are cryptographic security techniques that allow secure data exchange without revealing secret information. This research study investigates and analyzes efficiency factors, robustness features, applicability, and uses, along with challenges for the implementation of these techniques, which are most important to achieving higher security. We categorize ZKPs techniques into three types: interactive, non-interactive, and succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs). Different authors have examined prominent models such as zkSNARK, Ligero, Bulletproofs, Hyrax, Aurora, and Libra. Libra stands out for its outstanding efficiency, requiring a one-time trusted setup depending on the input size. The study explores various challenges in ZKPs to enhance their robustness. To solve problems like the trusted setup dilemma and quantum computing attacks, the research suggests making progress by integrating different models, improving efficiency, looking into new mathematical problems, creating more advanced cryptographic tools, and studying lattice-based cryptography for better security. The results highlight the need to overcome constraints and improve ZKPs security and effectiveness in practical setups to enhance their efficiency, and they will direct future research for privacy, security, and integrity in a variety of applications.

articleTitle: Approach to Post Quantum Cryptography Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: This paper outlines the procedure for validating cryptographic modules that implement Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) algorithms. It highlights public key encryption schemes, particularly PKE as well as the Module Lattice based Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) for CRYSTALS Kyber, both of which are included in the proposed standard NIST FIPS 203. The validation process entails submitting test vectors to the Implementation Under Test (IUT), aligning with NIST's validation methods, akin to those used for various FIPS approved algorithms like AES and SHA3. These PQC algorithms can be implemented by the vendors across various platforms, including hardware, software, and firmware. The test vectors generated act as basis for the Cryptographic Module Validation Testing (CMVT) to authenticate encryption components that incorporate these PQC algorithms.

articleTitle: Advanced QKD Protocols and Practical Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is an emerging field in private key cryptography. Recent advancements in quantum cryptography are focused on developing more secure protocols, particularly in response to the real time implementations of quantum hacking. Our research article focuses on Measurement-Device-Independent (MDI) and Twin-Field (TF) Quantum Key Distribution protocols, addressing the challenges associated with their implementation. We have discussed the implementation of a discrete phase randomization technique and phase slicing for Twin-Field (TF) Quantum Key Distribution, along with the integration of a random number generator (RNG). In our work, we designed and implemented initial quantum state preparation and the control electronics for an advanced Quantum Key Distribution system using an FPGA board.

articleTitle: On the Comparative Study of Recent Information Set Decoding (ISD) Attacks for QC-LDPC Code-Based McEliece Cryptosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: Code-based cryptography is one of the main candidates in quantum-resistant cryptographic techniques. LEDAcrypt is a code-based cryptographic scheme submitted in the 2nd round to the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) postquantum cryptography contest. Information set decoding (ISD) attacks, first introduced by Eugene Prange, are well-known non-structural attacks used effectively for code-based cryptography. After several improvements of the basic ISD algorithm, Stern's ISD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(ISD_{Stern})$</tex> and two recent improvements by Finiasz and Sendrier's ISD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(ISD_{FS})$</tex> and May, Meurer and Thomae's ISD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(ISD_{MMT})$</tex> draw significant attention. This paper demonstrates a detailed security analysis of key-recovery attacks using ISD and a comparative study of three ISD algorithms concerning the QC-LDPC-based McEliece cryptosystem variant of LEDAcrypt. Additionally, we have updated the LEDAcrypt parameter table from the original submission, incorporating two new parameters based on the ISD analysis. Simulation results show that the computational cost of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ISD_{MMT}$</tex> is lower than the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ISD_{Stern}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$ISD_{FS}$</tex> when applied for LEDAcrypt.

Author Keywords: Quasi-Cyclic low density parity check matrix (QC-LDPC)

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hybrid Cryptosystems for Secure Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: Traditional encryption systems, such as DES and Triple DES, face challenges when applied to images due to their high redundancy and large size. To address these challenges, this paper explores secure image encryption by comparing two hybrid cryptosys-tems, AES-256-GCM-SHA384 and ChaCha20-Poly1305-SHA256. Implemented locally in Python, these systems use the Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) algorithm for key exchange and their respective algorithms for bulk encryption, similar to those used in TLS 1.3. This work evaluates the performance and security of these systems using metrics including Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structural Similar-ity Index (SSIM), entropy, total encryption/decryption process time, Number of Pixel Change Rate (NPCR), Unified Average Changing Intensity (UACI), correlation coefficients, and Bit Error Rate (BER). A dataset of 10 satellite images is used for testing. The results show that AES-based cryptosystems outperform ChaCha20-based systems in speed, and both exhibit robust security features. Visual analysis, histogram, and correlation plots further validate the strength of the encryption. The paper concludes with proposed future research directions, including analysis of various image types, integration of post-quantum cryptography, and exploration of lightweight cryptography for resource-constrained PKI environments.

articleTitle: PKI-Enabled Authentication and Encryption for Enhanced Drone Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: In the realm of modern drone communication, where the exchange of sensitive data is ubiquitous, the assur-ance of authentication, confidentiality and integrity stands as paramount. This research paper delves into the application of Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) as a robust cryptographic frame-work to fortify the communication channels utilized by drones. Through a comprehensive exploration of PKI's mechanisms, this paper elucidates its role in ensuring the confidentiality of trans-mitted data through encryption and the preservation of integrity via digital certificates and authentication processes. Drawing upon theoretical foundations and practical implementations, this paper underscores the critical importance of PKI in safeguarding drone communication against eavesdropping, tampering, and unauthorized access. Furthermore, it examines contemporary challenges and emerging trends in PKI integration within drone networks, offering insights into potential avenues for future research and development. Drones are now essential instruments in several fields, such as emergency response, surveillance, and agriculture. Nonetheless, protecting drone communication from manipulation, illegal access, and data breaches is crucial. In addition to PKI, this paper explores the specific roles of certificate pinning and key pinning in enhancing drone communication security. Both techniques serve to further solidify the trust and authenticity of the communication endpoints, providing additional layers of protection. The purpose of this paper is to examine how PKI protects the authentication, integrity, and confidentiality of drone communications. The significance of PKI in strengthening the security posture of drone systems is emphasized by this research through an extensive examination of the body of literature and an analysis of PKI deployment options.

articleTitle: Distributed Estimation Based Public Key Infrastructure for In-Vehicle Network Security
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: Automotive Electronic Control Unit (ECU) security is a challenging problem due to over-the-air updates, cloud services, peripherals from third parties, and other third-party interfaces. In these scenarios, alongside the security triad (confi-dentiality, integrity, and availability), entity identity also becomes crucial to secure vehicles. This paper presents distributed estimation for the public key infrastructure (DE4PKI) technique which enhances the PKI framework with an encryption scheme that uses distributed estimation and cipher text. The main idea is to establish identity using PKI whereas data encryption uses a symmetric key alongside distributed estimation of CPS ciphertext to verify attacked nodes. The technique provides multiple layers of security through dynamic graphs, CPS variables, and PKI framework. It helps identify attacked nodes and eliminate them without hardware interventions and re-issuance of certificates once the ECUs are recovered from the attack. The distributed estimation framework provides scalability and localizes the at-tacks. The proposed technique is demonstrated on a typical ECU topology in a vehicle.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Entity On-Boarding and Authentication in Zero-Trust Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Public Key Infrastructure and its Applications (PKIA)
abstract: The zero-trust security model enhances enterprise security through proactive and real-time security strategies. It assumes that no entities within or outside the network are inherently trustworthy. Therefore, the authentication of users is given strong importance in a zero-trust system, such that, only authenticated entities can be allowed access to any of the resources of a zero-trust system. Very often, during the authentication process, verification of the digital certificates of the entities is considered indispensable. In this paper, we illustrate how the entities are registered and on-boarded into a zero-trust system using an integrated approach by the Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and Identity and Access Management System (IAMS). The IAMS in a zero trust system can maintain the user attributes and credentials to offload some of the activities of registration authority in the PKI. We emphasize the generation of a digital certificate for the user during the registration process. Therefore, we have demonstrated the simple steps for building a Certificate Authority (CA) of the PKI of zero trust system using the Open Source Secure Sockets Layer (OpenSSL) tool, which generates the digital certificate for valid users/devices during the registration or entity onboarding. Besides, we demonstrate the authentication based on the digital certificate in the zero trust system by the Policy Enforcement Point (PEP) using its IAMS and authentication server. We show here the effectiveness of a coordinated and integrated PKI, AIMS, and PEP in user/entity onboarding, digital certificate generation, and authentication for a zero-trust system.
